item.title: Future Payment Systems & Infrastructure Senior Associate
item.description: Job title: Future Payment Systems & Infrastructure Senior Associate Department: Payment Systems Market Interventions Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £67,200 and London from £59,200 to £73,800 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate, Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Katie via Katherine.Baker@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the PSR and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. Follow this link to find out more About The PSR. Operationally the PSR is currently an independent subsidiary of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), however in March 2025 the Prime Minister announced that the PSR would be consolidated into the FCA, a pragmatic next step in simplifying regulation of payments. This transition will likely take some time and will follow a Government consultation, although the Government has already been clear that payment systems must continue to be effectively regulated. For the time being, therefore, the PSR continues to focus on delivering its important and impactful programme of work, collaborating closely with the FCA. The Future Payment Systems and Infrastructure team you are applying to join will ultimately move into the FCA when the new legislation takes effect. Candidates should be aware, therefore, that there may be changes to their responsibilities as consolidation into the FCA progresses. This is an exciting opportunity to join the PSR's Future Payment Systems and Infrastructure team, helping to shape the future of the UK's retail payments landscape. The role will support the PSR's contribution to the National Payments Vision, engagement with new and emerging payment systems, and the development of a consistent, transparent regulatory approach as oversight transitions into the FCA. Working closely with other authorities, industry participants and senior stakeholders, you will play a key role in regulatory cooperation, policy delivery and influencing the future oversight of payment systems to support better outcomes for consumers, businesses and the wider economy. Role responsibilities Working in collaboration with other authorities and payment systems participants on key issues for the National Payments Vision Contributing to the PSR’s approach to new and developing payment systems Building a deep understanding of payment systems including emerging models, their operating environments, business strategies and governance arrangements Using this understanding to contribute to robust regulatory assessment and the delivery of improved outcomes for users of payment systems Building effective working relationships with key internal stakeholders and teams whose work is material to delivery of the team’s work Promoting a culture of collaboration, inclusion and learning within the Supervision team, acting as a role model for PSR values and behaviours Skills required Minimum: Experience in a regulatory, supervisory, monitoring, compliance, policy or similar environment, with evidence of managing stakeholder relationships and contributing to regulatory, policy or compliance-related outcomes Experience analysing complex information and making recommendations, demonstrated through written reports, briefings, policy papers, assessments or similar outputs that informed decisions or actions Understanding of payment systems and/or the broader payments landscape, including how payment systems operate and support effective regulation Essential: Experience leading or taking ownership of complex projects, workstreams or policy initiatives, demonstrating accountability for delivery and outcomes Demonstrated skill in working with internal and external stakeholders, building effective partnerships and negotiating toward strategic goals Demonstrated ability to resolve complex strategic or operational problems, including identifying root causes, evaluating options and delivering proportionate, evidence-based solutions Knowledge of the economic regulation, competition and/or payments landscape, including an understanding of how regulatory frameworks impact firms, consumers and market outcomes Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical, regulatory or policy issues clearly to diverse audiences and senior stakeholders Sound judgement and decision-making capability, demonstrated through balancing risks, evidence and stakeholder considerations in challenging or ambiguous situations Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results, including planning, organising and reprioritising work to meet deadlines and quality standards Effective project management skills, including coordinating activities, managing delivery against plans and ensuring objectives are delivered within agreed timescales Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page. Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. item.title: Lead Associate Lawyer
item.description: Lead Associate Lawyer Division: Legal Division Department: Law, Policy and International, Enforcement Legal Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £69,700 to £86,900 and London from £76,600 to £95,500 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Lead Associate - Practising legal Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Fizah via fizahfarouk.ibrahim@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. Our Legal Division provides advice and legal services across the full breadth of FCA activity, including regulatory, policy, enforcement and operational work. This Lead Associate position is in the Law and International team, which is part of the Law, Policy and International Department within Enforcement Legal. The department provides strategic, legal and policy advice on enforcement powers and policies and international enforcement engagement. The Law and International team owns the FCA’s strategy on international enforcement matters and is responsible for managing and developing key international enforcement relationships. We advise on, among other matters, the use of FCA investigation powers on behalf of overseas authorities, the disclosure of confidential information and the disclosure of personal data in an international enforcement context. The team also provides policy input on cooperation aspects of domestic legislation and legal advice on MoU work. Our associates are expected to engage with wider, cross-departmental enforcement policy work where needed. Role responsibilities Work with FCA investigation teams to advise on seeking assistance abroad and the use of evidence obtained abroad in civil, criminal and regulatory investigations and proceedings Perform initial reviews of requests for assistance received from overseas regulators. Your role is to identify all key legal issues, determine which FCA stakeholders should be made aware of the request and determine who at the FCA should respond to the request Build experience of managing more junior associates and their work. You will be expected to ensure that this work is managed and progressed effectively and to sign off key decisions for the exercise of legal powers Provide meaningful contributions to the department’s know how and guidance documents and training across the FCA, working together with the manager to ensure that legal risks are appropriately managed and work to become a specialist in agreed areas Have overall responsibility for the relationship management of several key international partners and internal stakeholders, building, maintaining and owning the relationships. This will involve regular discussions and development of a strategy to promote effective engagement, for example arranging visits and engaging others across the FCA Act as representative of Enforcement/Legal Division to senior managers and at international level, where appropriate, to ensure that the FCA’s interests are effectively represented Be accountable for advancing multiple key projects identified in collaboration with the team manager and department head. These are likely to involve complex legal issues and span the breadth of Law and International’s remit Where business need arises, associates in Law and International will work on projects relating to the wider remit of the Law, Policy and International Department Skills required Minimum: Qualified lawyer, Solicitor or Barrister of England and Wales or international equivalent Significant post-qualification experience in any of the following areas: contentious financial services or other regulatory investigations or proceedings; financial services or public law advisory work; international cooperation; complex international investigations Essential: Ability to apply sound principled legal and evidential analysis to novel situations and think strategically Well-developed relationship management skills to build and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues, international counterparts and external bodies Robust, self-motivated and a good team player Ability to perform effectively in demanding situations and meet deadlines Effective communication skills to present the outcome of analysis clearly and effectively, orally and in writing Real interest in international work, cross-border cooperation and enforcement policy Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Hybrid model where employees work a minimum of 40% in the office each month (expectation of 50% for senior leaders). Changing from September to a minimum of 50% in the office each month (expectation of 60% for Directors and Executive Directors) A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. item.title: Agentic Payments Technical Specialist
item.description: Agentic Payments Technical Specialist Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Payments and Digital Assets Policy Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £74,900 to £88,966 and London £82,300 to £97,800 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Technical Specialist – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via Steve.Christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Jennifer Wishart via Jennifer.Wishart@fca.org.uk . About the FCA and Team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Payments Policy Team is a large and growing team that works closely with HMT Treasury, and colleagues across FCA and PSR, to modernise the payments regulatory framework. This includes work to realise the benefits of agentic payments, whilst maintaining a safe and trusted payments system. The payments policy team sits in Payments & Digital Assets Policy, alongside teams working on tokenised payments and crypto policy. Role Responsibilities Collaborate with teams across the FCA to lead policy work on agentic payments, shaping proposals that will directly support innovation, and impact consumers and industry Apply your deep technical expertise in agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and its application to payments to the development of FCA policy and strategy both for domestic as well as international use cases for agentic payments Lead engagement with key stakeholders by building strong relationships with government, other domestic and international regulators, consumer groups, and technical experts in industry and beyond, to help shape the future of payments regulation Provide expert insight by delivering impactful advice and briefings on issues relating to agentic payments to colleagues and senior management Grow your expertise further, by developing deep knowledge of payments services and regulations and leading FCA thinking on the risks and opportunities of agentic AI and agentic payments Coach, mentor, and develop talent across the FCA, building analytical and risk management capabilities that elevate organisational performance Role model FCA values as part of the senior leadership team, fostering a culture of integrity, collaboration, and excellence Skills Required Minimum Significant professional experience in the application of agentic AI in payments Proven experience presenting complex issues clearly and succinctly to senior leaders and stakeholders, both orally and in writing Demonstratable experience of building and managing constructive relationships with key internal and external stakeholders Essential Evidence of leading complex projects, requiring strong problem solving and organisational skills, and the ability to manage a variety of competing priorities and issues An inclusive team player with experience of teaching, coaching and/or mentoring colleagues Demonstratable experience of engaging internationally on issues relating to regulation and innovation Benefits 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our Values and Culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability Confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. item.title: PA in Insurance ED and Directors Office - Insurance Supervision
item.description: LEEDS BASED Insurance Supervision The PRA's Insurance Supervision Directorate is the largest Directorate in the PRA. We supervise over 500 UK insurance firms and branches of international insurers across life insurance, general insurance and specialist supervision. Insurance plays a vital role in supporting households, businesses and the wider economy, providing financial security and resilience when it is needed most. The sector is grappling with some of the biggest challenges facing society, from climate change and cyber risk to changing demographics, long term investment for growth, and technological innovation. As insurers adapt their business models to meet these challenges, our work continues to evolve too, making Insurance Supervision a fascinating place to work at the intersection of risk, policy, supervision and strategy. We are committed to being a high-performing, inclusive and supportive Directorate where colleagues can build fulfilling careers, develop deep expertise and make a meaningful impact on the safety and soundness of the UK financial system. Role Responsibilities A core part of the role will be the provision of high-quality administrative and business support to the Director of Insurance Supervision, to the Senior Technical Advisor and to the Private Secretary while also being part of the wider office team in supporting the wider ED & Director Office team assisting with in delivering events and key Directorate activities. We're looking for someone who is organised, approachable and proactive, with excellent communication and administrative skills. You'll enjoy managing competing priorities, working at pace and providing a high-quality service, while building strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders. The role offers a unique perspective on the breadth of work taking place across Insurance Supervision. You'll work closely with senior leaders and colleagues across the Bank, while also engaging with external stakeholders including regulated firms, industry bodies, other regulators and partner organisations. You will be part of a strong and supportive PA community, with opportunities to learn, grow and build relationships across the Directorate. The breadth of the role, combined with the exposure you'll gain to senior leaders and external stakeholders, makes it an excellent platform for future career development. Role Requirements Minimum criteria Experience using the common Microsoft suite of IT programmes such as Outlook, Excel, Word, Loop, CoPilot etc Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. Strong organisational, administrative and time management skills and attention to detail. Proven ability to prioritise effectively and deliver under pressure. Essential criteria Knowledge of the PRA, Bank of England or wider financial services sector. Excellent judgement and decision-making capability. Strong strategic awareness and the ability to connect the dots across complex issues. Strong influencing and relationship-building skills, including with senior stakeholders. Experience of developing and supporting people. Evidence that you can quickly pick up new and complex technical issues. Absolute discretion, integrity and professionalism. Ability to work constructively within a team. Desirable criteria Knowledge of Insurance or Supervision of the Bank of England Experience working in or covering in an ED Office / Private Office An established network across the Insurance Directorate. Understanding of governance, business planning and strategic delivery. A desire to improve processes by using technology to enhance efficiency and ways of working. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Salary is circa £25,760-£28,000. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. (1) The application questions and (2) a single interview. This role closes on 29 September 2026. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

Our vision is to be the PRA’s trusted partners in delivering innovative technology and data products that empower PRA colleagues with advanced tools for enhanced decision-making, effective oversight and driving operational efficiencies. RDI is made up of 3 hubs: Strategy and Innovation Hub AI and Analytics Hub Delivery and Governance Hub This role is part of the Delivery and Governance Hub on a 9-12-month maternity cover secondment. item.title: Head of Department (x2 roles), Wholesale and Unauthorised Business Investigations
item.description: About the FCA At the FCA, we’re creating a fair and more resilient financial system. We’re establishing more transparent relationships between financial services and customers, building trust in financial markets and protecting vulnerable consumers. We’re currently on an exciting journey as we drive forward significant organisational, people, process, and technology transformation to become a more forward-thinking, proactive regulator. We will use data more effectively to drive better regulatory decisions and build greater cohesion across our broad financial services remit. Significant improvements in digital enablement, business intelligence, market data and information management maturity are all being pursued to maintain our position as a world leader in financial services regulation. In March 2025, the FCA launched a new 5-year strategy to deepen trust, rebalance risk, support growth and improve lives. The FCA will focus on four priorities: Be a smarter regulator ; predictable, purposeful and proportionate. The FCA will improve its processes and embrace technology to become more efficient and effective. Support sustained economic growth, by enabling investment, innovation and ensuring the continued competitiveness of the UK’s world-leading financial services. Help consumers navigate their financial lives by working with industry to boost trust, product innovation and ensuring the right information and support is available for people to take financial decisions. Fight financial crime, focusing on those who seek to use the fact they are regulated to do harm. It will go further to disrupt criminals and support firms to be an effective line of defence. Background We are looking to appoint two additional Heads of Department to help lead our Wholesale and Unauthorised Business Investigations (WUBI) directorate, joining the leadership team which is made up of two other Heads of Departments (HoDs) and the Director. Our efforts help to fight financial crime, disrupt harm, protect the interests of consumers, and ensure that markets work well and operate with integrity. WUBI conducts forensic investigations into regulatory breaches and criminal offences by firms and individuals operating in the wholesale arena, as well as those carrying on regulated activities without authorisation, in breach of the general prohibition. Typical WUBI cases include insider dealing, market manipulation, individual misconduct, fraud and scams, and organised crime activity linked to the financial services sector. The portfolio includes regulatory and criminal operations, civil proceedings and the FCA’s Proceeds of Crime team sits within WUBI. By working across the FCA and with domestic and international regulators and law enforcement, WUBI helps ensure a coordinated and effective response to threats facing UK markets and consumers, and disrupting criminal activity. The Role Reporting to the Director of WUBI, the Heads of Department ( HoDs) will be responsible for the development and delivery of the Enforcement strategy, in particular through ensuring investigations are delivered to a high standard. They will also play a key role in driving forward the FCA’s strategic work to fight financial crime and disrupt harm. The appointed candidates will be part of the Division’s senior leadership team and will take an active role supporting and challenging others to deliver the full range of the Division’s responsibilities (which also include Market Oversight and Intelligence). The candidates will be innovative, forward-thinking leaders who look across organisational boundaries, join up our work and drive forward the outcomes that matter most. Key responsibilities: Working with other Enforcement HoDs as part of a team to support the Director of WUBI in the delivery of the FCA’s work. Setting the strategic direction of the department (and with other senior management contributing to the strategic direction of the Division). Leading and inspiring a diverse, multi-disciplinary team of investigators. Promoting a culture of high performance, relying on coaching, influencing, and negotiating skills with a range of internal and external stakeholders Active management of a complex portfolio of investigations across WUBI to tight timeframes and which result in criminal, regulatory and civil action. Demonstrating clear operational grip and ensuring cases are delivered fairly, effectively and efficiently Collaborating across organisational boundaries to disrupt harm as early as possible, especially in relation to financial crime. Being accountable for divisional budget and resource management decisions as part of the senior divisional leadership team. What will the candidates get from the role? The successful candidates will: join the FCA’s senior leadership team at an exciting period of change for financial services and its regulation. lead a department of talented and experienced people, working collaboratively on significant projects and programmes get exposure to a broad range of issues and will contribute to the leadership team of both Enforcement and Market Oversight and the FCA, helping to shape and influence the organisation’s strategy. Skills/Experience Required We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. (To learn more about the Disability Confident Scheme Click Here ) Minimum Sound technical understanding of the regulatory framework in the UK and the FCA's place within it, with knowledge of the FCA’s powers and policies in relation to investigation and enforcement activity including criminal investigations and prosecutions. Significant people management and leadership experience, with a demonstrated ability to guide, motivate, and inspire large teams, while addressing performance concerns to build high performing teams. Extensive experience leading and overseeing complex investigations, with demonstrated clear operational grip Senior stakeholder management skills, with experience influencing internally & externally, and working across organisational boundaries to deliver cross-organisation projects. Ability to develop and implement change and process efficiency/improvements, delivering value for money and innovation Essential A clear track record of leading teams to deliver results against business priorities. A developed understanding of the regulatory and political environment in which the FCA operates, and an ability to build in-depth knowledge in this area. Ability to manage demanding situations, robustness in the face of challenge and able to make practical and balanced decisions quickly. Proficiency in maintaining strong working relationships across different business areas and to set joint goals for delivery. Negotiation and influencing skills – to deploy internally and externally. Ability to work as part of a senior leadership team with a wide range of responsibilities, supporting colleagues and the Director in the delivery of their work. Understanding how intelligence supports efforts to prevent and respond to criminal activity. Budget management and experience of managing external resources. The FCA’s Values & Diversity Our ambition is to create a diverse and inclusive workplace that reflects the society we serve, helping us to be a better regulator. We serve the public and our decisions directly affect the wellbeing of people, businesses and the UK economy. So, our values matter. They represent the culture we aspire to every day, guiding our judgements, building trust and helping us to be ‘At our best’. The FCA is committed to achieving greater diversity across all levels of our organisation. Given this, we particularly welcome applications from women, disabled, and minority ethnic candidates, as under-represented groups. As an inclusive employer, we are open to considering flexible working arrangements, including job shares. Please inform your recruiter if you wish to apply for this role on a flexible basis. Application Support We want to remove any possible barriers and are committed to providing a wide range of reasonable adjustments so that you can keep the focus on your conversations and be at your best. If you have an accessibility requirement, disability, or condition that means you might require changes to the recruitment process, please contact your recruiter to discuss this further. Our aim is to make your application as easy as possible, and your recruiter will be happy to work with you to make any necessary arrangements where possible. Benefits Our competitive benefits scheme gives you the opportunity to create a personalised benefits package, tailored to suit your lifecycle. You can use this allowance to purchase additional benefits such as dental or cycle to work, or you have the option to top up your base salary by taking this as cash. Core benefits that you will receive as standard are: 30 days holiday per year plus bank holidays Private healthcare with Bupa A non-contributory Pension of at least 8% of basic salary each month (there are several contribution levels that increase depending on your age - up to 12% a month once you reach age 35) Life assurance of eight times your basic salary Income protection Conflicts of interest All applicants to the FCA are required to demonstrate that they do not have other interests likely to conflict with their responsibilities as an employee of the FCA. You should declare any potential conflict of interest as early as possible in the selection process, and also disclose information or personal connections that, if appointed, might be open to misperception. Any potential conflicts of interest will not prevent candidates going forward to interview but may, i

item.title: Senior Credit Rating Agency Supervision Associate
item.description: Job Title: Senior Credit Rating Agency Supervision Associate Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Infrastructure and Exchanges Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £67,200 and London £59,200 to £73,800 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via steve.christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Iona Magee via iona.magee@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK. We are currently seeking a skilled individual to join the Benchmarks and Credit Rating Agencies Supervision team within the Capital Markets Department. The Capital Markets Department sits within SPC division at the FCA and is responsible for both benchmark and credit rating agencies supervision and policy. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Benchmarks and Credit Ratings Supervision Team is responsible for supervising UK-regulated benchmark administrators and CRAs in line with the applicable regulatory requirements and the FCA’s Approach to Supervision. Benchmark administrators produce benchmarks that are used across financial markets. Where they perform this role effectively, market participants can rely on accurate and representative measures of underlying market activity. CRAs play a key role in providing an assessment of the creditworthiness of governments, corporates and other issuers of securities. Where they perform this role effectively, investors are well-informed on the risks of investing in these assets and hence, capital is more efficiently allocated. These outcomes contribute particularly to the FCA’s statutory objective for market integrity and its consumer protection objective. Role responsibilities Lead the FCA’s supervisory relationships with assigned CRAs, using engagement and direct dialogue to support positive behavioural change and deliver effective regulatory outcomes Shape and deliver strategic supervisory initiatives across ratings processes, operational resilience and governance, helping to reduce harm and improve market integrity Apply expert judgement to identify emerging risks within credit ratings markets and support proportionate interventions that protect consumers and enhance confidence in the financial system Build close partnerships with senior stakeholders across the FCA, bringing insights together to inform supervisory priorities and decision-making Share expertise and contribute to a collaborative learning culture, supporting colleagues across Capital Markets and enhancing the FCA’s supervisory effectiveness Work closely with colleagues across supervisory teams to identify risks, solve complex challenges and deliver outcomes that help safeguard markets and improve the financial wellbeing of millions of consumers across the UK Skills required Minimum: Prior experience working in a regulatory or financial services position, such as credit rating agency, commercial or investment bank, asset management, law firm or any other regulatory body Prior experience working in an analytical role using a varied range of information, both qualitative and quantitative and using that to form judgements that balance a range of factors Essential: Thorough understanding of the CRAs business model, credit ratings processes and the potential risks associated with CRA activities Ability to lead and deliver projects effectively within agreed timelines while managing multiple priorities Effective verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present clear, concise and well-reasoned arguments Ability to make informed and timely decisions, acting on their own initiative to identify key issues, navigate complexity and escalate matters where appropriate Well-developed organizational skills, with the ability to balance competing priorities and manage changing demands effectively Flexible and responsive approach, with the ability to respond positively to change and adjust working styles to meet evolving business needs Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively as part of a team, consistently supporting colleagues and contributing to the successful delivery of shared objectives Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Job advert close: 22nd September 2026 at Midnight CV Review/Shortlist: 24th September 2026 1st stage Interviews: w/c 5th October 2026 2nd stage Interviews: w/c 19th October 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time

item.title: Public Affairs and Campaigns Adviser
item.description: Location: Westminster Contract : Fixed term for 6-12 months Salary: £47,609 per annum (Including London Weighting) About us The Local Government Association (LGA) is the national membership body for local authorities. We work on behalf of our member councils to support, promote and improve local government. We are a politically led, cross-party organisation that works on behalf of councils to ensure local government has a strong, credible voice with national government. We influence and set the political agenda on the issues that matter to councils to help them deliver local solutions to national problems. We also provide councils with the tools and resources to respond to challenges present and emerging, and support improvement across the sector. We value diversity and encourage applications from all sections of the community to this high-profile role. About the role Reporting to the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement, duties of the Public Affairs and Campaigns Adviser include: *Work collaboratively as part of the Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement team to contribute to the development and delivery of the LGA’s public affairs and campaigns activity. This will involve working with colleagues across the LGA to enhance the political influence and public profile of both the LGA and local government. *Contribute to the delivery of the LGA’s Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement approach by helping to influence parliamentary debates, select committees and legislation in order to secure positive change on behalf of local government. * Support delivery of the LGA’s Communications Strategy by building and maintaining key relationships in Parliament and with other relevant corporate stakeholders. *Support LGA councillors and member councils to engage with Parliament, including briefing senior LGA members and officials ahead of parliamentary inquiries and as part of the LGA’s party conference engagement. This will also involve working closely with the LGA’s Chair and members of the Senior Leadership Team. *Work with the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement to organise high-impact public affairs events and ensure the LGA has a strong corporate profile at the autumn party conferences. This includes organising high-impact briefings to build the LGA’s network of support in Parliament, supporting the LGA’s annual local government parliamentary reception and organising Smith Square Debates. *Provide perceptive and insightful political intelligence and advice to identify opportunities for the LGA, strengthen the organisation’s public affairs profile and support wider communications activity. *Work with the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement and colleagues across the Communications Directorate to provide public affairs advice and support to member councils, including through the LGA’s Public Affairs Network. * Support the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement in ensuring that the Public Affairs team is the first point of contact for queries from MPs, peers, political parties, parliamentary staff, think tanks and stakeholders on LGA policy recommendations and local government issues. Promote and enhance the reputation of local government and, where necessary, help defend councils’ reputation. *Work with colleagues, as required by the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement, to produce regular forward-looking grids summarising, scheduling and coordinating future LGA public affairs and campaigning activity, announcements and other initiatives. *Undertake out-of-hours duties as necessary, including attending parliamentary, political, think tank and campaign-related events. The position is required to support immediate delivery needs The organisation is consulting on its operating model The grade and responsibilities are subject to confirmation Priority consideration may be given to employees at risk where they have the required qualifications and experience About you Based in the LGA’s office in Westminster, the Public Affairs and Campaigns Adviser will have: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, be highly motivated and able to work using your own initiative. An interest in developing your own networks within both political and communications circles. A strong commitment to personal and professional development achieved by maintaining regular communication with contacts in Parliament, Whitehall and stakeholders relevant to local government. Strong interpersonal skills and a proactive, team-oriented approach to working. A keen interest in networking and confidence to communicate with members of parliament, government ministers and officials, and leaders across local government. Considerable experience working for a parliamentarian, select committee, government department or delivering public affairs in a lobbying/campaigning organisation or within local and regional government. You must have the right to work in the UK, the LGA are unfortunately unable to offer sponsorship visas. Evidence for the right to work in the UK will be requested at the interview stage. Please note that, due to the nature of the role, applications from current serving councillors cannot be considered. To apply If you would like to be considered for the role, please complete the online form and include a supporting statement detailing how you meet the criteria for the role before the closing date. We are specifically assessing candidates against the following criteria: 1. Considerable experience working for a parliamentarian, select committee, government department or delivering public affairs in a lobbying/campaigning organisation or within local and regional government. 2. An excellent understanding of Westminster, Whitehall and local government, including the interface between local authorities, national government, political parties and opinion-formers. 3. Experience and evidence of success in positively influencing relevant opinion-formers, including influencing primary legislation, a parliamentary debate, a select committee report or working with parliamentarians to secure the tabling of parliamentary questions. 4. Evidence of success in working to deliver public affairs plans and corporate campaigns. 5. Experience in aligning public affairs and campaigning activity with colleagues in other disciplines, including media, policy and campaigns. 6. Ability to prioritise competing demands, within a pressured environment, and adopt a flexible approach to work and - when necessary - working hours. Closing Date: 01 October 2026, 5pm Interview Date: TBC We use anonymous recruitment, which is the practice of hiding candidates’ identities. This process involves removing any identifying information from candidates’ applications which includes names. At the LGA we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees where everyone is treated with dignity and respect. Our recruitment decisions are based on fair, open competition, with appointment on merit. ***The LGA are proud to be awarded a “Disability Confident Leader”. Please contact us via *** Recruitment@local.gov.ukif you require a reasonable adjustment, which is a change to the format or conditions of the recruitment process to accommodate any disability-related needs you may have. Our benefits LGA annual leave entitlement is 29 days, rising to 31 days after three years’ service and to 33 days after five years’ service, plus all UK public holidays (pro rata for fixed term and part time contracts).* Flexible & agile working – office-based staff are required to work in the LGA’s London office two days per week as a minimum, subject to business need and this may vary significantly between different roles and from week to week. Future development – face-to-face and virtual courses are scheduled in line with developmental goals The LGA offers 24/7 access to a free, confidential employee assistance programme managed by Health Assured. This service is also available for Dependants. Family friendly policies For more of LGA’s benefits and working with us, please view our webpage https://www.local.gov.uk/benefits-and-working-lga Our values & behaviours Our Values and Behaviours are there to give us an understanding of who we are as an organisation and who we want to be. They are a framework to help us understand: how we work with each other how we work with our members and stakeholders our expectations for ourselves and each other Our values are: Collaboration – We value collaboration, to pursue shared goals by encouraging and utilising diverse perspectives and working with internal and external colleagues across the organisation. Inclusion – We value inclusion, where everyone feels valued, understood, and supported to contribute meaningfully. Ambition – We value ambition, reflecting our desire to achieve best possible outcomes for local government, communities, and individuals. Respect – We value respect, to ensure fairness, recognition, and shared accountability.

item.title: Head of Department: AI & Technology Security Operations
item.description: The FCA has retained Global Resourcing to manage this role; send applications directly to Global Resourcing . About the FCA At the FCA, we’re creating a fair and more resilient financial system. We’re establishing more transparent relationships between financial services and customers, building trust in financial markets and protecting vulnerable consumers. We’re currently on an exciting journey as we drive forward significant organisational, people, process, and AI and technology transformation to become a more forward-thinking, proactive regulator. We will use data more effectively to drive better regulatory decisions and build greater cohesion across our broad financial services remit. Significant improvements in digital enablement, business intelligence, market data and information management maturity are all being pursued to maintain our position as a world leader in financial services regulation. In March 2025, the FCA launched a new 5-year strategy to deepen trust, rebalance risk, support growth and improve lives. The FCA will focus on four priorities: Be a smarter regulator; predictable, purposeful and proportionate. The FCA will improve its processes and embrace technology to become more efficient and effective. Support sustained economic growth, by enabling investment, innovation and ensuring the continued competitiveness of the UK’s world-leading financial services. Help consumers navigate their financial lives by working with industry to boost trust, product innovation and ensuring the right information and support is available for people to take financial decisions. Fight financial crime, focusing on those who seek to use the fact they are regulated to do harm. It will go further to disrupt criminals and support firms to be an effective line of defence. The Role We have an exciting opportunity for a permanent Head of AI & Technology Security Operations. This role is designed for an experienced manager, senior technical specialist, or existing Head of Department with proven experience of leading teams and operating at scale in a rapidly evolving digital and AI-driven operating environment. The successful candidate will strengthen their strategic and operational leadership while overseeing high-tempo, service-critical digital and AI operations. The Head of AI & Technology Security Operations is accountable for ensuring that the FCA’s technology estate — including rapidly expanding AI capabilities — is robust, secure, and able to withstand, detect, and recover from disruption, failure, or exploitation. The role brings together operational resilience, infrastructure governance, supplier oversight, and enterprise technology and AI-specific vulnerability management, ensuring that both traditional infrastructure and AI-enabled systems are designed, operated, and governed to remain safe, dependable, and trustworthy under stress. Working in close collaboration with C&IR (Cyber and Information Resilience), this HoD plays a critical leadership role in implementing and managing the technology controls needed to anticipate and mitigate AI-driven risks, including model vulnerabilities, upstream dependency risks, data poisoning, adversarial attacks, and control failures arising from increased autonomy and scale. This role will be responsible for leading, motivating and directing the department (~70FTE) across London, Leeds, & Edinburgh; and managing the FCA’s critical Digital and AI systems, including AI live service, Service Desk, Incident Management, Cyber Security Operations and Supplier Management. This is a fantastic development opportunity which will help to build expertise, experience and career skills in a senior, challenging and highly visible role. The role will be reporting to the Chief Information Officer, and sit in the wider Data, Technology, and Innovation Division. What will the candidate get from the role? As Head of AI & Technology Security Operations, you will join the DTI senior leadership team at a pivotal moment in the FCA’s evolution, supporting its ambition to become a forward-thinking, AI-enabled and data-driven regulator. You will lead a skilled multidisciplinary department, working across high-impact digital and AI initiatives to strengthen technology and AI risk management, improve resilience and enable the safe adoption of emerging technologies. Collaborating closely with Cyber & Information Resilience, DTI leadership, product teams and front-line divisions, you will play a key role in driving meaningful change and reinforcing the FCA’s reputation as a trusted, innovative regulator. Key responsibilities will include: Leading the development and operation of the FCA’s AI vulnerability and threat management capability, identifying and mitigating risks linked to AI model weaknesses, adversarial threats, automation and agentic AI systems. Establishing clear frameworks and controls for the safe deployment of AI, including human oversight, monitoring, explainability, version control, containment and safe shutdown mechanisms. Maintaining effective AI governance, including ownership, inventory management, risk classification and oversight of AI-enabled services across the organisation. Acting as accountable owner for technology and AI risk, including control design, testing, assurance activity and risk acceptance decisions. Providing clear, metrics-led reporting to senior committees and Board-level forums on risk posture, emerging threats, control effectiveness and material gaps. Overseeing critical third-party and AI supply chain dependencies, including cloud platforms, AI model providers, managed services and data sources. Ensuring supplier, concentration and substitution risks are understood, monitored and managed effectively. Owning technology continuity strategies across data, digital and AI services, ensuring critical services can withstand disruption, degrade safely and recover effectively. Overseeing scenario testing, failover design, recovery validation and core service operations, including incident, problem and change management. Leading and developing multidisciplinary teams across technology risk, AI operations, supplier management, continuity and live service operations. Building strong capability, clear accountability and a culture where secure, resilient and dependable systems are a shared responsibility. Representing the FCA externally with government, regulators, industry bodies and standards organisations on technology, AI and operational resilience. Managing team budget, headcount, resources and IT supplier spend of approximately £80m. Championing innovation, continuous improvement and the safe adoption of emerging technologies to strengthen resilience, efficiency and value for money. This is a high-profile leadership role with enterprise-scale accountability, operating at the intersection of AI, cyber, technology, supplier and operational risk, with a direct contribution to the FCA’s regulatory credibility and public trust. Skills/Experience Required We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer, and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. (To learn more about the Disability Confident Scheme Click Here ) Minimum Hands on experience, however recent, with AI or agentic AI technologies. Familiarity with UK regulatory frameworks relating to operational resilience, critical third parties, cyber resilience, and AI governance. Experience within financial services, government, regulatory, or other highly regulated environments Essential Strong stakeholder management, capable of engaging with and developing strong trusting relationships with stakeholders from across a business organisation and at senior levels, as well as third parties. Evidence of managing supplier relationships across a complex supplier and contract environment Knowledge of NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, ISO 27001, DORA, or similar frameworks. An ability to manage and control risk, embed good practice, and drive change where necessary. In-depth working knowledge of multiple domains, including Engineering, DevOps, AI, Cyber Security and Cloud technology platforms. Experience of driving change and process efficiency/improvements, delivering value for money and innovation. Ability to inclusively lead a large group of talented individuals with a wide variety of professional expertise, experience, and backgrounds. The FCA’s Values & Diversity Our ambition is to create a diverse and inclusive workplace that reflects the society we serve, helping us to be a better regulator. We serve the public and our decisions directly affect the wellbeing of people, businesses and the UK economy. So, our values matter. They represent the culture we aspire to every day, guiding our judgements, building trust and helping us to be ‘At our best’. The FCA is committed to achieving greater diversity across all levels of our organisation. Given this, we particularly welcome applications from women, disabled, and minority ethnic candidates, as under-represented groups. As an inclusive employer, we are open to considering flexible working arrangements, including job shares. Please inform your recruiter if you wish to apply for this role on a flexible basis. As part of the FCA’s on-going commitment to develop our national presence, most of our vacancies are now open to working in our Edinburgh, Leeds or London offices. This means that as part of the application process you will be able to select your preference of which office location you would like to work from. Application Support We want to remove any possible barriers and are committed to providing a wide range of reasonable adjustments so that you can keep the focus on your conversations and be at your best. item.title: Programme Manager – SEND
item.description: Location: Home based Contract : 8 month secondment or FTC Salary: £78,551 to £89,005 About us The Local Government Association (LGA) is the national membership body for local authorities. We work on behalf of our member councils to support, promote and improve local government. We are a politically led, cross-party organisation that works on behalf of councils to ensure local government has a strong, credible voice with national government. We influence and set the political agenda on the issues that matter to councils to help them deliver local solutions to national problems. We also provide councils with the tools and resources to respond to challenges present and emerging, and support improvement across the sector. We value diversity and encourage applications from all sections of the community to this high-profile role. About the role The LGA is seeking to appoint a programme manager with experience of working in SEND system, within local government at a senior, strategic level. Working closely with senior colleagues within the LGA with responsibility for the children’s services improvement programme you will act as a key interface between the LGA and local authorities and their partners. You will lead the delivery and implementation of a Department for Education grant focussed on leadership development in SEND. You will work with key sector partners, including local authorities, DfE, ADCS, health, education settings and parents/carers, to design and deliver improvement activity that strengthens leadership capacity in local SEND systems. Your success will be determined by your ability to understand and respond to the highly challenging, politically sensitive and high-profile SEND environment in order to manage complexities and risk, and successfully maintain a positive reputation for the LGA with its member authorities. About you * You will have a comprehensive understanding about how local areas, through multi agency arrangements, provide services for children with SEND and the complexities, challenges and opportunities this presents. * You will have a comprehensive understanding of local government and the wider public sector and how the delivery of services for children sits within this. * You will be confident and credible in working with leading members, chief executives, directors of children’s services and other partner system leaders * You will hit the ground running, using your abilities and experience to effectively manage and maintain relationships with local authorities and the Department for Education to ensure effective delivery of the children’s improvement programme. You must have the right to work in the UK, the LGA are unfortunately unable to offer sponsorship visas. Evidence for the right to work in the UK will be requested at the interview stage. To apply If you would like to be considered for the role, please complete the online form and include a supporting statement detailing how you meet the criteria for the role before the closing date. We are specifically assessing candidates against the following criteria: * Proven knowledge and expertise in relation to the national policy context affecting SEND services * Record of achievement in complex political environments, in local government SEND services * Understanding of the key issues, priorities and pressures affecting local government including the policy and improvement agenda * Political sensitivity, and the ability to exercise appropriate discretion and judgement on issues of significance and importance, and when dealing with politicians and officials * Practical experience of designing interventions and innovative solutions to complex issues affecting SEND * Confident and resilient with excellent people skills, able to develop positive internal and external relationships; Strong team player able to build alliances and lead from within To help us anonymise applications efficiently, please ensure your CV meets the following formatting requirements: * Please use standard fonts such as Arial, Times New Roman, or Calibri * Avoid complex graphics, logos, or images where possible * Keep formatting simple – use basic bullet points and standard paragraph formatting * Save your CV as a standard PDF file * Ensure the file size is under 5MB * Avoid unusual page layouts or multi-column designs * Use standard text colours (e.g., black, or dark grey) CVs that do not meet these guidelines may not be processed correctly by our system. Closing Date: 5pm, 24 September Interview Date: week commencing 28 September, interviews will be virtual Interview Panel: TBC We use anonymous recruitment, which is the practice of hiding candidates’ identities. This process involves removing any identifying information from candidates’ applications which includes names. At the LGA we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees where everyone is treated with dignity and respect. Our recruitment decisions are based on fair, open competition, with appointment on merit. The LGA are proud to be awarded a “Disability Confident Leader”. Please contact us via Recruitment@local.gov.uk if you require a reasonable adjustment, which is a change to the format or conditions of the recruitment process to accommodate any disability-related needs you may have. Our benefits LGA annual leave entitlement is 29 days, rising to 31 days after three years’ service and to 33 days after five years’ service, plus all UK public holidays (pro rata for fixed term and part time contracts).* Flexible & agile working – office-based staff are required to work in the LGA’s London office two days per week as a minimum, subject to business need and this may vary significantly between different roles and from week to week. Future development – face-to-face and virtual courses are scheduled in line with developmental goals The LGA offers 24/7 access to a free, confidential employee assistance programme managed by Health Assured. Family friendly policies For more of LGA’s benefits and working with us, please view our webpage https://www.local.gov.uk/benefits-and-working-lga Our values & behaviours Our Values and Behaviours are there to give us an understanding of who we are as an organisation and who we want to be. They are a framework to help us understand: how we work with each other how we work with our members and stakeholders our expectations for ourselves and each other Our values are: Collaboration – We value collaboration, to pursue shared goals by encouraging and utilising diverse perspectives and working with internal and external colleagues across the organisation. Inclusion – We value inclusion, where everyone feels valued, understood, and supported to contribute meaningfully. Ambition – We value ambition, reflecting our desire to achieve best possible outcomes for local government, communities, and individuals. Respect – We value respect, to ensure fairness, recognition, and shared accountability.

item.title: Banking and Securities Operations Technician - specialist in Market Settlement Team, 12-month opportunity
item.description: About the team The Market Settlements Team (MST) team sits within the Central Banking Operations Division and is responsible for the safe, accurate and timely settlement of securities and cash flows arising from activity determined by Foreign Exchange Division (FED) and Sterling Markets Division (SMD). The team settles a wide range of products, including repos, bond trades, swaps and futures related cash movements and reconciliations, alongside cash funding, collateral management and asset servicing activity including coupons and maturities. MST supports activity across the Bank’s own foreign currency reserves and the Exchange Equalisation Account (EEA) managed on behalf of HM Treasury. About the Role As a Technical Specialist, you will provide subject matter expertise across securities settlement, cash funding, asset servicing custody, and selected derivative products. The role combines direct operational involvement with technical expertise, supporting the accurate and efficient processing of securities and cash movements in a highly controlled environment. You will apply technical expertise to resolve non-standard settlement and asset servicing issues, provide advice and guidance on operational matters, and support a strong risk and control environment by identifying and mitigating operational risks in line with established procedures and governance. Alongside business-as-usual responsibilities, the role offers opportunities to support change initiatives and continuous improvement activity that strengthen delivery across the team and the wider Central Banking Operations Directorate. What You’ll Do 1. Specialist Operational Delivery Deliver and maintain the timely and accurate settlement of securities and cash movements, ensuring compliance with industry standards, market conventions and legal deadlines. Apply detailed knowledge of core banking, payment and securities systems (including Openlink, SWIFT Alliance Access, T24, Fedwire, Euroclear and Clearstream) to support effective end‑to‑end processing, issue resolution and control of settlement activity. 2. Technical Leadership & Issue Resolution Investigate and resolve operational and system related issues, working closely with internal teams to ensure timely and effective resolution. Act as an escalation point for complex operational queries and time critical decisions. Provide technical expertise across the team, acting as a point of reference, mentor and support for colleagues. 3. Change, Testing & Continuous Improvement Support the implementation of change initiatives, including requirements, testing and system releases. Identify and drive process improvements to increase automation, resilience and control effectiveness. Promote operational excellence and a culture of continuous improvement. 4. Controls, Risk & Incident Management Maintain strong operational controls across settlements Support incident assessment by providing clear technical insight on root cause, impact, and remediation and lessons learned. 5. Data, MI & Relationship Management Produce and analyse management information to identify trends, support decision making, and evidence control effectiveness. Act as a key point of contact for stakeholders, including Front Office areas, custodians and counterparties Build and maintain effective working relationships, representing the team in internal and external forums. Role requirements To be considered for this role, candidates must meet all the minimum criteria: Minimum Criteria Demonstrable operational experience and strong working knowledge in at least one of the following areas: securities settlements, collateral management, asset servicing, swaps, and/or futures related cash and reconciliation activity. Proven ability to deliver high quality, well controlled outputs within a regulated operational environment. Strong problem-solving capability, including identifying issues, assessing impacts, and proposing practical resolutions. Essential Criteria Well- developed analytical skills, including the ability to interpret data and make sound, evidence-based recommendations. Ability to understand end to end operational impacts of decisions and changes. Effective organisational and workload management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and work accurately under pressure. Ability to adapt to changing information, anticipating risks and opportunities. Strong interpersonal and communications skills, with the ability to engage effectively with internal and external stakeholders at both junior and senior levels. Proficiency with Excel and other Microsoft applications. In addition to the minimum and essential criteria, candidates will typically demonstrate one or more of the following: Desirable Criteria Broader operational exposure across multiple product areas, with working knowledge in two or more of: securities settlements, collateral management, asset servicing, swaps, or futures. Working knowledge of core banking, payments and securities and data systems/applications: Openlink, SAA / SWIFT, T24, EasyWay, Xact, R, Tableau, Python, PowerBI. Experience delivering change initiatives or working on projects within an operational environment. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information Location: London This role offers an annual salary range in circa. of £39,360 - £44,280 (depending on skills and experience). In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two stages. This role closes for applications on 01 October 2026. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.
